headline: Mirza Fakhrul set to become 23rd President of Bangladesh as BNP submits nomination
summary: The former BNP Secretary General's election is almost certain due to the party's overwhelming majority in parliament, ending a 35-year streak of uncontested presidential polls.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, former Secretary General of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), is poised to become the 23rd President of Bangladesh. His nomination paper was submitted yesterday as the ruling BNP's candidate, making his election virtually assured due to the party's significant parliamentary majority.

This development marks a potential end to 35 years of uncontested presidential elections in Bangladesh. While an 11-party alliance candidate, Col (retd) Oli Ahmad, also submitted a nomination, the numbers in parliament heavily favor Mirza Fakhrul.

The last time a presidential election was contested was in 1991. Since then, seven presidents have been elected unopposed. The current 13th Jatiya Sangsad has 349 members, with BNP holding 247 seats compared to the 11-party alliance's 90.

According to the election schedule, nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16, with the withdrawal deadline set for August 18. If two valid candidates remain, voting will take place on August 20 in the Jatiya Sangsad session room.

Mirza Fakhrul resigned from his posts as BNP Secretary General and Standing Committee member after being nominated. He served as the party's Secretary General for nearly 16 years, playing a critical leadership role during challenging periods for the BNP.

His nomination was finalized during a meeting called by BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman at the Prime Minister's office. Senior BNP leaders Abdul Moin Khan and Gayeshwar Chandra Roy acted as proposer and supporter for his nomination, respectively.

headline_marked: [[Tanzid Hasan Tamim scores maiden Test ton]] as Bangladesh dominate Australia in Darwin Test
headline: Tanzid Hasan Tamim scores maiden Test ton as Bangladesh dominate Australia in Darwin Test
summary: Tanzid Hasan Tamim made history by becoming the first Bangladeshi to score a Test century on Australian soil, helping Bangladesh secure a 32-run lead over Australia on Day 2 of the opening Test in Darwin.
details: Tanzid Hasan Tamim struck his maiden Test ton as Bangladesh continued to dominate against Australia on the second day of the opening Test in Darwin on Friday. This significant achievement propelled Bangladesh into a strong position, taking an early lead in the match.

Tanzid completed his hundred off 188 balls, featuring eight fours and a six. This historic knock made him the first Bangladesh batter to score a Test ton on Australian soil, and only the second Bangladeshi to achieve a Test hundred against Australia.

Before Tanzid's century, skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto also completed his seventh Test fifty in the same over. Bangladesh reached 230 for two in their first innings, taking a 32-run lead over Australia, who were bowled out for 198.

The Tigers had taken the lead earlier when Tanzid cut Mitchell Starc for a boundary, surpassing Australia's first-innings total. Tanzid and Mominul Haque built a crucial 102-run stand for the second wicket, followed by a 76-run partnership between Tanzid and Shanto.

Australia, fielding their full-strength side, utilized six bowlers. Starc, Josh Hazlewood, and Pat Cummins bowled the majority of overs. Bangladesh remains in a strong position, with key players like Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das still to bat.
On Day 1, Hasan Mahmud's career-high six-for helped bowl out Australia for 198. Bangladesh ended the first day at 96 for one at stumps, setting the stage for their dominant performance on Day 2.
